questions.q: What is an Architecture Decision Record (ADR), per this lesson?
options: A standard, structured, written record capturing a significant architecture decision's context, options considered, and reasoning behind the choice made
A ServiceNow-specific configuration table stored on the instance
A log of every update set deployed to production
A meeting invite sent before a decision is discussed
questions.explain: An ADR is a structured written record of context, options, decision, and consequences — a practice used across the software industry generally.

questions.q: Why does this lesson emphasize that ADRs are a software-industry-wide practice, not a ServiceNow-specific idea?
options: Because it means ADRs don't apply to ServiceNow architecture decisions at all
Because it means the discipline of writing ADRs is a transferable skill usable on any platform you architect for
Because ServiceNow actually invented the ADR format
Because it means ADRs are optional and rarely used anywhere
questions.explain: The lesson notes this explicitly: because ADRs are a general software-architecture practice, the skill transfers beyond ServiceNow.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say recording rejected options is often the most valuable part of an ADR?
options: Because rejected options are legally required to be documented
Because it lets a future reader see that an odd-looking choice was a real tradeoff against a specific alternative, not an oversight
Because rejected options are more interesting to read than the final decision
Because the chosen option is never actually recorded in a real ADR
questions.explain: Without knowing what alternatives were weighed and why they lost, a later reader can't tell a deliberate tradeoff from a mistake.

questions.q: What real, practical problem does this lesson say an ADR prevents?
options: A sound decision being second-guessed or reversed by someone who never knew the original constraints that justified it
An instance running out of storage space
A developer writing code outside their assigned scope
A certification exam expiring before it's renewed
questions.explain: Without a durable record, the reasoning behind a decision fades from memory, and a later reader may reverse it without understanding why it was made.

questions.q: According to this lesson, when should an architect write an ADR for a ServiceNow architecture decision?
options: Only after the decision has caused a problem years later
Never — ADRs are not useful for ServiceNow-specific decisions
While the reasoning is still fresh, naming the real context and even the options that were rejected
Only if ServiceNow support requests one
questions.explain: The whole value of an ADR depends on capturing the reasoning before it's forgotten — so it should be written at the time the decision is made.
